hub.title: Customs
hub.tagline: Pay the right duty. Not a franc more, not a franc less.
hub.intro: On a single real customs declaration, four items out of ten were misclassified: a voltage "regulator" declared as a refrigerator, chairs as furniture, new clothes as second-hand clothing. These tools show what you really owe, before you buy.
hub.simulatorDesc: What customs will charge for a product, line by line, before you buy.
hub.searchDesc: Using market words: hair extensions, second-hand clothes, okada, 手机…
hub.walletCardDesc: Simulate a product's duties and taxes before paying your supplier.
hub.facts: The calculations reproduce the CAMCIS assessment to the franc on real declarations.
hub.classifyDesc: The assistant proposes the HS code, a licensed customs broker signs it.

notes.freight_missing: Freight is not counted. Customs adds it to the value: every franc of freight is taxed like the goods.
notes.vehicle_other_rule: The 2026 finance law provides {{rate}}% excise for this vehicle (CAMCIS still applies the former rule): {{total}} F of duties and taxes instead of {{current}} F.
notes.tec_40: The ECCAS common tariff in force since 1 January 2026 may raise this product to 40%: that would be {{total}} F instead of {{current}} F. Have the rate confirmed in the CAMCIS integrated tariff.
notes.phones: Phones: the 2023 finance law (art. 7) provides a 50% abatement on the value, and CAMCIS links the tax to the IMEI since 2026. Not applied here: confirm with your declarant.
notes.env_tax_plastic: Environmental tax on plastic articles (2026 finance law): 5% of the value, capped at 1,000 F per unit. Not counted here.
notes.insurance_estimated: Insurance estimated at 0.5%: insurance of imported goods is compulsory in Cameroon, with a locally licensed insurer (law no. 75-14).
notes.precompte_niu: Without a NIU, the précompte is 10% instead of 2% for a company on the real regime. A tax ID (NIU) is free at the tax office.
notes.di_rvc: Above 2,000,000 F FOB: import declaration (DI) on e-GUCE before shipment, then SGS verification certificate (RVC). Without them, the fine is 25% of the value (2026 finance law).
notes.sgs_invoice: Ask your supplier to upload the final invoice to export-cm.sgs.com as soon as the goods ship. Without it, SGS may retain a value three times higher — it happened on a Toyota Fortuner: 2,311,829 F too much.
notes.domiciliation: Above 5,000,000 F, the import must be domiciled with a bank. Pay your supplier with Bonzini: the payment proof establishes the price actually paid (CEMAC customs code, art. 30).
notes.code_check: Check that the code on the declaration describes your goods, not a word that looks like it: a "regulator" declared as a refrigerator cost 35,779 F too much on 150,000 F.

files.homeTagline: The right HS code, signed by a licensed customs broker.
files.how1Desc: In your own words, with photos of the goods and their rating plate.
files.how2Desc: It asks the questions that decide between codes, then proposes one to three codes, with its reasons and the duty of each.
files.how3Desc: They approve or correct it. The signed code becomes your reference, and you can ask customs to confirm it (advance ruling).
files.name: The product
files.nameHint: What you call it: “5 kVA regulator”, “plastic chairs”, “hair extensions”…
files.descriptionHint: Material, use, how it works, power, new or used. Paste the supplier’s description if you have it.
files.photosHint: The rating plate and the composition label often decide between two codes.
files.privacy: The description and photos are read by our assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) and then by the licensed broker. They are used for this classification only.
files.none: Your classification files will appear here.
files.thinking: The assistant is searching the tariff…
files.signedTitle: Code signed by a licensed customs broker
files.atBrokerDesc: They are reviewing the file, the photos and the proposal. You will be notified as soon as they sign, or if they need more information.
files.needsInfoDesc: Answer at the bottom of the conversation, then send the file back.
files.submitDesc: A licensed customs broker checks and signs it. The signed code becomes your reference for the declaration.
files.submitCta: Have it signed by a licensed broker
files.submitSheet: They review the description, the photos and the conversation. They sign the code, correct it, or ask you a question. While they review, the assistant no longer answers on this file.
files.cancelSheet: The file stays in your list, but no one will answer it any more.
files.letterIntro: The CEMAC Customs Code (art. 75) lets you ask customs to confirm a classification before importing. The letter is in French, as filed with the Cameroon customs: fill in NIU, RCCM and address, sign it, and file it with the attachments.

review.title: Classification review
review.readOnlyShort: Only a registered licensed broker can sign.
review.noAi: The assistant made no proposal: the client sent the file directly.
review.notWaiting: This file is not awaiting a decision.
review.readOnly: Only a licensed customs broker can sign a classification. You are viewing the file read-only.
review.noLicense: Your licence is not registered yet. Ask an administrator to enter it on your team profile.
review.claimedByOther: Another broker is reviewing this file.
review.claimDesc: It leaves the other brokers’ queue. You can then sign, correct or ask a question.
review.nationalHint: The 8 or 12 digits of the CAMCIS line, if you know it.
review.askHint: The client gets it as a notification and answers in their file.
review.noteHint: The client reads it with the signed code.
review.noteWhy: Say why this code rather than the proposed one.
review.noteAsk: Tell the client what is missing.
review.signNotice: By signing, you commit your licence: your company and licence number appear on the client’s file.
